name: Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA ceilings)
title: Does a weak stress result cap what a bank pays out?
field: organization science, with roots in agronomy boundary lines (necessary-but-not-sufficient analysis)
what: Fits a ceiling on the scatter (no high outcome without enough of the condition) and measures the empty corner above it.
grade: contested (standard test cannot tell a ceiling from a correlation)
pick_line: Noise-robust isotonic-quantile ceiling tested against tail-dependent copula nulls with firm blocks, so no single firm sets the gate.
data: Public filings (Fed DFAST/CCAR results 2013–2025, FR Y-9C payouts, SCB); descriptive only
one: Stressed CET1 trough caps payouts beyond correlation; drawdown's apparent cap is correlation-made; SCB rarely binds.

picture.la: Usual tool: mean regression on the CET1 trough (R² 0.10)
picture.lb: NCA ceiling: empty corner, d = 0.25 (beyond correlation)

findings.h: The stressed CET1 trough caps payouts beyond what correlation explains.
findings.t: 360 firm-years: CE-FDH ceiling of payout/RWA on the SA minimum CET1 ratio, d = 0.245; within-year permutation p = 0.0002 (NCA package p = 0.0009); Gaussian-copula range of spuriousness at the observed ρ = 0.20: mean 0.16, 95th percentile 0.21, p = 0.012. Next-year payouts d = 0.38 (p = 0.0045). Dividends/RWA d = 0.43 (p = 0.016), net buybacks/RWA d = 0.24 (p = 0.011) although their rank correlation is 0.02. OLS on payouts: R² 0.10.
findings.note: Pre-registered finding (d ≥ 0.10, within-year p < 0.05, above the spuriousness 95th percentile) met for all four outcomes.

chart.la: Observed d vs what correlation alone gives

findings.h: The drawdown passes the standard NCA test, but only through correlation.
findings.t: Minus CET1 drawdown: d = 0.50, standard permutation p = 0.010 (package), within-year 0.013 — the usual reading is "necessary". But data with the same marginals and correlation (ρ = 0.30) and no ceiling give d of 0.49 on average (95th percentile 0.57; p = 0.48). On our data shape, the standard test calls such correlated-only data "necessary" in 73.5% of 200 simulations.
findings.note: Computed. This is the Sorjonen–Melin critique reproduced on bank data. The rejection rate is 3% at ρ = 0, 15% at 0.1, 38% at 0.2.

chart.title: Standard NCA test: share calling correlated-only data necessary (drawdown shape)

findings.h: Pre-tax income moves the average payout, not the cap.
findings.t: SA pre-tax income: OLS R² 0.16, quantile regression slopes at τ = 0.90 and 0.95 both p < 0.001, but ceiling d = 0.24 with within-year p = 0.76 and spuriousness p = 1.0. Loan-loss rate: no ceiling (p = 0.64) and no mean effect (R² 0.01).
findings.note: Together with finding 1: the trough decides who may pay a lot; earnings explain how much those above the gate pay.

chart.title: Pre-tax income: ceiling d vs correlation-only 95th percentile

findings.h: The trough is the binding limit for 69% of firm-years; the SCB for 1.5%.
findings.t: With the four pooled ceilings, the minimum CET1 is the limiting factor for 69% of firm-years, drawdown 16%, loan losses 5%, pre-tax income 4%, ties 7%. In 2021–2025 with the SCB added: trough 54%, SCB 1.5%; the SCB's own ceiling (d = 0.54) is not beyond chance (within-year p = 0.47, spuriousness p = 0.79).
findings.note: Liebig's law of the minimum, as in boundary-line yield-gap analysis. Ceilings are pooled over years.

findings.h: The gate tightened after 2020 and holds for each payout channel.
findings.t: 2013–2019: d = 0.31 (within-era p = 0.0005, spuriousness p = 0.079); 2020–2025: d = 0.36 (p = 0.0005, spuriousness p = 0.005). The trough seen among firms paying the era's median payout rose from 5.6% to 6.4%. Dropping the top 2% of the trough or of payouts: dividends and buybacks keep spuriousness p ≤ 0.015; total payout keeps it when payout outliers go (p = 0.014) but weakens to 0.082 when the best-capitalized 2% go. Leave-one-year-out: worst p 0.12.
findings.note: The era split and trims were added after N1 (labelled). Payout rules since 2020 link the SCB and payout limits to capital by design.

findings.h: As a next-year upper envelope it is too loose.
findings.t: Walk-forward 2015–2025 (312 firm-years): CE-FDH ceiling broken by 7.1% with mean headroom 2.04 pp of RWA; QR τ = 0.95: 6.4%, 1.42; OLS + 1.645 s: 9.0%, 1.23; ARDL(1,0) 95%: 11.6%, 0.71; SARIMAX(1,0,0)+exog 95%: 13.2%, 0.62.
findings.note: Pre-stated bar (violations ≤ 10% with headroom no larger than the quantile line) failed on headroom. NCA describes the frontier; it is not a forecaster.
